title: Overconfidence Detector
dataSources: Forecasts (`prediction:forecast`), resolved outcomes (`prediction:outcome`), personal bets (`bet:personal`), calibration scores (`calibration:score`), Brier scores (`brier:score`).
app: Personal forecasting and calibration — a private prediction journal of dated forecasts about your own life, resolved outcomes, and calibration / Brier scoring — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=prediction:outcome confidence>=90
| stats avg(eval(if(result="correct",1,0))) as hit_rate, count as n
| eval hit_pct=round(100*hit_rate,1), overconfidence_gap=round(95-hit_pct,1)
description: Checks the predictions you were almost certain about and measures how often you were actually right.
value: Overconfidence is the most common judgement error; measuring your own gap is the first step to fixing it.
implementation: Ingest high-confidence forecasts into `index=personal`; compare claimed confidence to the real hit rate.
visualization: Single-value panel of the overconfidence gap.
grandmaExplanation: It checks the things you were absolutely sure about and shows how often you were actually right.
